name.text: Finding the mistake in a vector calculation

questiontext.text:
Wanjiku was asked to find \({@p@}\mathbf{a} - {@q@}\mathbf{b}\), where \(\mathbf{a} = {@ta@}\) and \(\mathbf{b} = {@tb@}\). Her working has one mistake.

  • Step 1: \(\mathbf{a} = {@cv3(A)@}\), \(\mathbf{b} = {@cv3(B)@}\)
  • Step 2: \({@p@}\mathbf{a} = {@cv3(s2)@}\)
  • Step 3: \({@q@}\mathbf{b} = {@cv3(s3)@}\)
  • Step 4: \({@p@}\mathbf{a} - {@q@}\mathbf{b} = {@cv3(s4)@}\)
  • Step 5: So \({@p@}\mathbf{a} - {@q@}\mathbf{b} = {@sh@}\).

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Give the correct value of \({@p@}\mathbf{a} - {@q@}\mathbf{b}\) in i, j, k form.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) [[if test="is(er=2)"]]Step 2 is wrong: a scalar multiplies every component, so \({@p@}\mathbf{a} = {@cv3(c2)@}\).[[/if]][[if test="is(er=3)"]]Step 3 is wrong: a scalar multiplies every component; it never adds to them. \({@q@}\mathbf{b} = {@cv3(c3)@}\).[[/if]][[if test="is(er=4)"]]Step 4 is wrong: subtracting a negative component adds its size. Component by component, \({@p@}\mathbf{a} - {@q@}\mathbf{b} = {@cv3(okl)@}\).[[/if]]

(b) \({@p@}\mathbf{a} = {@cv3(c2)@}\), \({@q@}\mathbf{b} = {@cv3(c3)@}\), so \({@p@}\mathbf{a} - {@q@}\mathbf{b} = {@cv3(okl)@} = {@okv@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Vectors II: finding the mistake in a vector calculation

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.6: Find the wrong step in a worked combination of three-dimensional vectors and give the correct result.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: ch: if is(ans1 = "s2") then 2 elseif is(ans1 = "s3") then 3 elseif is(ans1 = "s4") then 4 else 0;

truefeedback.text: Step 5 only rewrites step 4 in i, j, k form. The mistake is earlier: check each component in steps 2, 3 and 4.
Step 1 is right: those are the columns of \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\).

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(ch=2)"]]

Step 2 is right: \({@p@}\) times each component of \(\mathbf{a}\) gives \({@cv3(c2)@}\). Check steps 3 and 4 the same way, one component at a time.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ch=3)"]]

Step 3 is right: \({@q@}\) times each component of \(\mathbf{b}\) gives \({@cv3(c3)@}\). Check steps 2 and 4 the same way, one component at a time.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ch=4)"]]

Step 4 subtracts the column in step 3 from the column in step 2 correctly, so no new mistake is made there. One of those two columns is already wrong: multiply out \({@p@}\mathbf{a}\) and \({@q@}\mathbf{b}\) yourself and compare.

[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is Wanjiku's answer, which contains the mistake.
That is \({@q@}\mathbf{b} - {@p@}\mathbf{a}\), the negative of the answer.

falsefeedback.text: Work out \({@p@}\mathbf{a}\) and \({@q@}\mathbf{b}\) component by component, then subtract matching components.
